newsitem.title: USA: Woman convicted in nationwide US prostitution ring.
newsitem.headline: Woman convicted in nationwide US prostitution ring.

text.p: A federal jury has convicted a New York woman of running a nationwide prostitution ring in states including Florida, New Hampshire, Illinois, North Carolina, California, Ohio and Iowa, prosecutors said on Wednesday.
Federal authorities said the case was unusual because it was rare for a prostitution ring to operate on a national basis.

Agatha Mercedez Peets, 39, was convicted on Tuesday of five charges of carrying on a prostitution business in violation of the federal law prohibiting interstate travel in aid of a racketeering enterprise by a jury in White Plains, N.Y., prosecutors said.
She was also charged with one count of threatening one of her prostitutes if she did not pay Peets a commission.
Peets, who ran the ring out of New York City, faces a possible maximum sentence of 30 years in prison and a $250,000 fine on each of the six counts.
Prosecutors said that while it was unclear how many prostitutes worked for Peet, files of some 300 women were found during a search of the defendant's premises.
